problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

examples.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2 \,$ and $\, R_2 :=  R_2+(-1)R_1?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14080619/assets/e607bba88cc1f15abaa45fc3cf02110243433d60259c56805515ced373054ca0.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".
